outline.title: Pairing: a terminal starts the app
`request` (the first acting grant, built by this spec)
Widening, one grant at a time

line.text: status: draft   # written on 2026-11-14 from the operator's direction in a host session: "shouldn't we be able to launch in a secure scope even without user involvement by spawning the app from a terminal with a signed key exchange or similar? i agree to narrowing scope but i think we start narrow and expand explicitly in order to maintain secure operations and support a wide feature set in the app." The direction is the operator's; the design is not yet approved. It amends an operator decision (2026-10-25, spec 005 section 2.1), so only the operator can approve it.

spec.title: 120: The app scope: a key paired from a terminal, and grants that widen one at a time

summary.text:
| # | Observation (2026-11-14) |
| :-- | :-- |
| E-1 | The app attaches on the narrator socket and can only read. Anything the operator wants to do from a page (ask a follow-up, have a section researched further, rebuild a page, dispute a statement) is a command copied to the clipboard (117 §6). |
| E-2 | The daemon gives a scope by the socket a client connects to, checks the peer's user id, and issues an acting token only to a client at a terminal. A window has no terminal, so the app cannot be given one. |
| E-3 | The operator wants the app to carry a wide set of features over time, each added on purpose, without loosening what keeps the daemon safe. |
